speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition better, can you describe the appearance of the rash in more detail, such as whether it is raised, flat, or blistery? Also, did the rash appear before, during, or after the onset of your fever and cold symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the trunk rash have a characteristic "slapped cheek" appearance followed by a lacy, reticular pattern on the limbs? Has she received the MMR vaccine recently?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Mildly pruritic rash on trunk and extremities. I also have Low-grade fever, Rhinorrhea, Headache, Facial rash not involving the perioral skin.

speaker: Doctor
text: The clinical presentation of a facial rash sparing the perioral area followed by a reticular rash on the extremities is classic for Erythema Infectiosum. DIAGNOSIS READY: Fifth disease (Erythema Infectiosum) caused by Parvovirus B19
